title: README.rdoc documents the removed pre-1.0.0 API; every example is broken
description:
Commit ec6a5f3 rewrote lib/ and spec/ for 1.0.0 and deleted lib/log_switch/mixin.rb, but left README.rdoc untouched. Every documented idiom was tested against the shipped code and is broken:

| README shows | Reality in 1.0.0 |
| extend LogSwitch | Only 'include LogSwitch' works; extend defines no #log -> NoMethodError: undefined method 'log' for class MyThing |
| MyThing.log "msg" (class-level) | #log is an instance method — MyThing.new.log "msg" |
| LogSwitch::Mixin (documented at length, README.rdoc:102-160) | Removed in 1.0.0; LogSwitch.const_defined?(:Mixin) => false |
| MyThing.log = false | MyThing.logging_enabled = false |
| MyThing.log_level = :warn | MyThing.default_log_level = :warn |
| MyThing.before { } | MyThing.before_log = Proc.new { } |

This is the gem's front page on GitHub and rubygems.org, so a new user's first copy-paste raises NoMethodError. That makes it the highest-leverage fix in this backlog despite being docs-only.

README.rdoc:163-173 ('REQUIREMENTS') is also stale, advertising MRI 1.8.7/1.9.2/1.9.3, ree, JRuby 1.6.5, Rubinius 1.2.4.

spec/log_switch_spec.rb is the accurate description of the current API — use it as the source of truth when rewriting. Note that logging is off by default (logging_enabled defaults to false), which the README never mentions and which surprises anyone expecting output from a fresh includer.
design: Rewrite SYNOPSIS against the real API, delete the LogSwitch::Mixin section outright, refresh REQUIREMENTS. Run every example before committing — that is exactly the check that was skipped in ec6a5f3. Sequencing: the config epic (log_switch-aev) will change this same public API, so either rewrite twice or land that first; the docs are wrong either way, so do not let that block a fix.
acceptance_criteria: Every README example runs as written against the shipped gem and produces the documented output.

title: Config state leaks across includers — every class shares one slot
description:
ClassMethods stores config in class variables declared in the module body, so the variables belong to the ClassMethods module itself rather than to each including class. All includers therefore share a single config slot and stomp each other.

Verified:
  class A; include LogSwitch; end
  class B; include LogSwitch; end
  A.logging_enabled = true
  B.logging_enabled?  # => true   (B was never touched)

This directly contradicts History.rdoc:3-5, which advertises as the headline 1.0.0 improvement: 'LogSwitch can now be included in your own module, then that included in other modules. This allows toggling logging per includer.' That is not what the code does. The same false claim is what makes gh-5 look resolved when it is not — History.rdoc:8-10 cites the improvements above as alleviating it.

Affects @@logging_enabled, @@log_class_name, @@default_log_level, @@logger, and @@before_block alike. Since the gem's entire purpose is a per-class switchable logger, this defeats the point for anyone with more than one includer.
design: Real design change, not a tweak: move to ivars on the singleton class, or a class_attribute-style scheme with inheritance. Decide explicitly what should happen for a class that includes a module that included LogSwitch (the cascade path set up by LogSwitch.included) — per-class isolation and inherited defaults pull in different directions. Also decide whether LogSwitch.logger stays a global fallback. This is a breaking behavior change to a released gem; pair it with a version bump and a History.rdoc entry. Revisit gh-5 once done.
acceptance_criteria: Two independent includers hold independent config for every setting; a regression spec covers the A/B leak above.

title: log_class_name = false never sticks; '||=' reader flips it back to true
description:
lib/log_switch.rb:77-79 reads:

  def log_class_name
    @@log_class_name ||= true
  end

'||=' reassigns whenever the current value is falsy, so the value written by log_class_name=(false) is overwritten with true on the very next read. The setter is therefore inert and class names cannot be turned off.

Verified:
  class A; include LogSwitch; end
  A.log_class_name = false
  A.log_class_name  # => true

This is the cause of the spec at spec/log_switch_spec.rb:64, marked: pending "Can't figure out why this doesn't pass. It works live...". It does not work live — the reader is the bug. The pending annotation is misleading and should go with the fix.

logging_enabled (lib/log_switch.rb:43-45) has the identical '||= false' shape but is currently harmless, because its default is already falsy. It is a latent trap: anyone changing that default to true reintroduces this exact bug.
design: Use an explicit defined? check (or set the default once at include time) instead of '||=', so false is a storable value. Fix logging_enabled's reader at the same time even though it is not currently observable.
acceptance_criteria: A.log_class_name = false reads back as false; the 'pending' at spec/log_switch_spec.rb:64 is removed and the spec passes on its own merits.

title: Re-resolve dev dependencies; Gemfile.lock pins are a decade stale
description:
Gemfile.lock pins rspec 2.12.0, simplecov 0.7.1, tailor 1.1.2, diff-lcs 1.1.3, multi_json 1.4.0 — none of which resolve or build on current Ruby. Gemfile.lock also still records log_switch (0.4.0) while lib/log_switch/version.rb says 1.0.0, so the lock predates the 1.0.0 release.

The gemspec's conditional dev-dependency blocks are also vestigial: they branch on RUBY_VERSION > '1.9' and RUBY_ENGINE == 'ruby' to guard simplecov and tailor, which no longer means anything for supported Rubies.

Note the specs themselves are fine — they are written in rspec 2 style but use 'expect' syntax and pass unmodified on rspec 3.13.
design: Relax the gemspec dev deps (rspec '~> 3.13'), drop the RUBY_VERSION/RUBY_ENGINE conditionals, delete Gemfile.lock and re-resolve. Consider whether Gemfile.lock should be committed at all — for a library gem the usual convention is to gitignore it.
acceptance_criteria: 'bundle install' succeeds and 'bundle exec rspec' runs the suite to 18 examples / 0 failures on current Ruby.

title: Gemfile uses 'source :rubygems', which modern Bundler rejects outright
description:
Gemfile:1 reads 'source :rubygems'. Bundler 4 removed that form and errors before evaluating anything else:

  [REMOVED] The source :rubygems is disallowed because HTTP requests are insecure.
  Please change your source to 'https://rubygems.org' if possible, or 'http://rubygems.org' if not.

This is the first domino: it makes 'bundle install', 'bundle exec <anything>', and every rake task fail, since the Rakefile requires bundler/gem_tasks. Reproduce with 'bundle exec rake -T'.
design: One-line change to "https://rubygems.org". Cheap on its own, but it only surfaces the next failure (stale pins in Gemfile.lock) rather than producing a working install — hence the follow-up child.
acceptance_criteria: 'bundle install' gets past Gemfile evaluation and fails only on dependency resolution, if at all.

title: Correct documentation that describes a removed API
description: Commit ec6a5f3 ('Rewrite to simplify for 1.0.0') rewrote lib/ and spec/ and deleted lib/log_switch/mixin.rb, but never touched README.rdoc or reconciled History.rdoc. The published docs describe a pre-1.0.0 API that no longer exists, and a 1.0.0 feature claim that was never true.
acceptance_criteria: README examples are copy-pasteable against 1.0.0 and verified by running them; History.rdoc contains no false claims.

title: Fix config-state defects in LogSwitch::ClassMethods
description:
Three separately-observable bugs in the config layer of lib/log_switch.rb, all verified by execution. They share one root cause: config is stored in class variables (@@logging_enabled, @@log_class_name, @@default_log_level, @@logger, @@before_block) declared in the ClassMethods module body, and read back through memoizing '||=' accessors.

Because the @@vars live on the ClassMethods module itself, every includer shares one slot. Because the readers use '||=' against a truthy default, a stored falsy value can never be read back.
design: A single refactor most likely resolves all three children at once: move config off class variables onto per-includer state (ivars on the singleton, or class_attribute-style inheritance), and replace '||= default' readers with explicit defined?/nil checks so false is storable. Children are tracked separately because they are distinct user-visible defects that each need their own regression test, but expect to close them together. This changes published behavior of a released gem (1.0.0) — treat as a breaking change and decide on a version bump.
acceptance_criteria: Each child bug has a regression spec that fails before the refactor and passes after; no 'pending' specs remain in the suite.

title: Restore a working dev toolchain on modern Ruby
description:
The Bundler-based toolchain is dead on current Ruby (verified on ruby 4.0.5 / bundler 4.0.16). 'bundle install', 'bundle exec rspec', and every rake task ('rake spec', 'rake test', 'rake yard', default) fail before running any code. Until this is fixed there is no supported way to run the suite; the only working path is bypassing Bundler with the system rspec 3:

  ruby -Ispec -e 'require "rspec/core"; exit RSpec::Core::Runner.run(["spec"], $stderr, $stdout)'

That invocation does work today: 18 examples, 0 failures, 1 pending.
design: Two independent breakages stack here: the Gemfile source directive, and the ancient pins in Gemfile.lock. Fix the Gemfile first, then re-resolve. The tailor linter and Travis config are dead weight that can be handled separately.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, single-command way to run the suite works from a clean checkout without hand-editing files.

title: History.rdoc 1.0.0 entry claims per-includer toggling that was never implemented
description:
History.rdoc:1-10 says of 1.0.0: 'LogSwitch can now be included in your own module, then that included in other modules. This allows toggling logging per includer.' The include-cascade half is true (LogSwitch.included redefines base.included to propagate the mixin). The 'toggling per includer' half is false — config lives in shared class variables, so includers stomp each other. See log_switch-aev.3 for the verified reproduction.

The entry then cites those improvements as alleviating gh-5, so gh-5 is likely still open in practice.

Also worth noting for anyone reading the changelog: History.rdoc:7 records 'Removed LogSwitch::Mixin in favor of simpler implementation' — the changelog got this right while the README never caught up (log_switch-8h9.1).
design: Do not silently rewrite history. Either correct the 1.0.0 entry to describe only what shipped, or leave it and record the truth in the next release's entry once log_switch-aev.3 lands. Recheck gh-5 upstream.
acceptance_criteria: History.rdoc contains no claim contradicted by the code, and gh-5's real status is established.

title: before_log= silently discards every hook after the first
description:
lib/log_switch.rb:101-103 defines the setter with '||=' rather than '=':

  def before_log=(block)
    @@before_block ||= block
  end

Once any hook is set, every later assignment is silently ignored. A setter that discards its argument with no error is a quiet failure — callers have no way to notice.

Verified:
  C.before_log = Proc.new { puts 'FIRST hook' }
  C.before_log = Proc.new { puts 'SECOND hook' }
  C.before_log.call  # => prints 'FIRST hook'

The reader below it (before_log, lib/log_switch.rb:105-107) legitimately needs a no-op default, but that belongs in the reader, not the setter.

Not covered by the current suite: the spec at spec/log_switch_spec.rb:70-75 only ever assigns once, so it passes despite the bug.
design: Setter becomes a plain '@@before_block = block'; keep the empty-Proc default in the reader.
acceptance_criteria: Assigning before_log twice results in the second hook running; a regression spec asserts this.

title: Replace dead .travis.yml with working CI
description:
.travis.yml targets rvm 2.1.3, 2.0.0, jruby-19mode, and rbx-19mode. Travis CI no longer runs for this project and every listed Ruby is long EOL, so there is currently no CI at all — nothing would have caught the toolchain rot recorded in this epic.

The repo is on GitHub (turboladen/log_switch) and already merges Dependabot PRs, so GitHub Actions is the natural fit.
design: Add .github/workflows/ci.yml running the suite across supported Rubies; delete .travis.yml. Best done after the Gemfile/lock work so CI has something green to run.
acceptance_criteria: A CI run passes on push against at least one current Ruby, and .travis.yml is gone.

title: Remove or replace the tailor linter wired into 'rake test'
description:
Rakefile:15-24 conditionally defines a Tailor::RakeTask and makes 'rake test' depend on [:spec, :tailor]. tailor 1.1.2 is unmaintained and does not install on current Ruby, so it takes 'rake test' down with it.

Worth knowing: tailor depends on log_switch itself (see Gemfile.lock:24-25, 'tailor (1.1.2)' -> 'log_switch (>= 0.3.0)'). That circular dev dependency is real, not a misconfiguration.
design: Straight removal is the low-risk option; RuboCop is the modern replacement if linting is still wanted. Either way the RUBY_ENGINE/RUBY_VERSION conditional around it in both Rakefile and gemspec should go.
acceptance_criteria: 'rake test' runs to completion without tailor.
